newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Cricket's Young relieved wait is over.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Cricket's Young relieved wait is over.

text.p: Bryan Young felt huge relief when he was named in place of unfit Blair Pocock in the New Zealand cricket team to tour Sharjah and Pakistan from next month, NZPA reported.

Young has been on standby for fellow opener Pocock since the squad was first named on September 22 but his Northern Districts team-mate only recently lost his race to recover from surgery on his right shoulder.
Young, 31, had continued to attend training camps as Pocock's understudy and admitted yesterday the hardest part had been the "waiting and uncertainty".
"It's a great feeling to be back. I missed it when I was dropped last season."
Young said he had never given up hope of an international recall despite falling out with former coach Glenn Turner and fellow selectors Rick Pickard and Mike Shrimpton last summer.
"I stayed positive because I love the game. I'm starting my 14th first-class season and I wouldn't carry on if I didn't enjoy it."
Young has played 18 tests, scoring 1052 runs at 30.05, and has also appeared in 47 one-day internationals. He last played for New Zealand on December 23 last year, against Pakistan in Auckland.

With Nathan Astle and Craig Spearman having established themselves as New Zealand's opening combination, Young may find himself batting at No. 3, especially with there being a desire to drop Stephen Fleming down to No. 4, just ahead of Mark Greatbatch.
Pocock's shoulder injury affected his throwing action and ability to throw from long distance.

New Zealand coach Steve Rixon, who is placing a premium on fielding and fitness, said Pocock would have been unable to field on the boundary and would have had slower reactions than normal fielding inside the circle.

"Blair is only able to throw about 50 metres and he is also restricted in his sideways throwing action which could mean in one-day cricket an extra run being scored," said Rixon, who felt Pocock would be better served by remaining at home and playing in the domestic first-class season.
"Blair's put in a lot of work rehabilitating the shoulder. But he is not going to be 100 percent fit for the tour."
National selection panel convener Ross Dykes said he was hopeful Pocock would be a contender for a place in the New Zealand team to play England in January and February.
Pocock is the second tour casualty, following last week's withdrawal of medium-pacer Chris Pringle with an ankle injury. He was replaced by Auckland allrounder Justin Vaughan.
The inclusion of senior seamer Danny Morrison, who is recovering from a groin operation, will be known after he completes two training matches in Christchurch this week.
